ONE STEP

Send the form and a person reads it. Nothing has to be verified first.

Submit your tool

Every submission is read by a person against your own site. Questions? alston@aitoolsmarketer.com

How to Submit an AI Tool

Submitting a tool takes a couple of minutes. The review that follows is the same one every entry on the list goes through, whether we found it or you sent it in.

Check it fits. Read the four checks below and the two questions the form asks about marketing. A tool that is live, built for a marketing job and has published pricing is almost always a fit.
Fill the form. The tool and its website, the marketing job it does, the problem it solves, how a team uses it, and an email we can reply to. AI Auto-fill can draft most of it from your own home page.
Say how you would like to launch. One question at the end of the form tells us what to write back: a faster launch or the standard editorial queue. Press Submit and you are done: nothing else has to happen before it reaches us.
We review it. A person reads the submission, then researches the tool from its pricing page, documentation and changelog, the same way every entry on the list is researched.
You hear back. We email you within 24 hours with where your submission stands. You get a reply either way, including when the answer is no.
What AI Tools You Can Submit

Any AI software a marketing team would pay for, including generative AI tools for writing, images and video. Every entry is filed under the marketing job it does, so the quickest way to know whether yours fits is to find its job below:

AI Search, GEO and AEO Tools
AI SEO and Keyword Research Tools
AI Content and Copywriting Tools
AI Ad Creative Tools
AI Advertising and Media Buying Tools
AI Video and Image Generation Tools
AI Social Media Marketing Tools
AI LinkedIn and X Growth Tools
AI Social Listening and Community Outreach Tools
AI Creator, Influencer and Short-Form Video Tools
AI Landing Page and Lead Capture Builders
AI CRO, Personalization and ABM Tools
AI Email Marketing and Deliverability Tools
AI Marketing Automation and Lifecycle Tools
AI Marketing Analytics and Reporting Tools
AI Market Research and Competitive Intelligence Tools

If your tool does a marketing job that is not on this list, submit it anyway and say which job it does. If it is not built for marketers at all, it is likely to be declined, and we will tell you so.

WHAT GETS LISTED
Four Things We Check

Reading these before you send the form is the fastest way to know whether it is worth your time.

It is released and usable

Anyone can sign up and use it today. A waitlist, a demo video or a landing page with an email capture on it is not yet a product we can describe.

A marketer would recognise the job

The tool does something a working marketing team would pay for: content, search, ads, social, lifecycle, analytics, creative, or the operations around them.

Pricing is published

A public pricing page, or plan limits stated somewhere we can link to. "Contact us for pricing" on its own leaves nothing to record in the entry.

The claims can be checked

Feature and limit claims trace back to documentation, a changelog or the pricing page. We cite sources on every entry, so anything we cannot source does not go in.

What the Launch Question Changes, and What It Does Not

The last question on the form asks how you would like to launch. It changes what we write back to you: which options we send, and how soon. It does not change the entry.

Everything on a page here is written from the vendor's own pricing page, documentation and changelog, and it says what those sources say. No option buys a position either: the list runs newest first, which is the date an entry joined rather than a judgement about it, and nothing on this site is scored or ranked. Entries are not sent to vendors for approval.

The same rules are set out in the editorial policy and how we compile this list, which apply to every submission alike.

What Happens After You Submit

This site is a compilation rather than a review board. The tool list has no scores, no verdicts and no ranked order, so a submission is not a competition you either win or lose. It is a pointer at a tool we might not have found, and what happens next is research.

We read it, then we go and look

The answers you send tell us where to look. The entry itself is written from the pricing page, the documentation, the changelog and whatever independent coverage exists, because those are the things a reader can check for themselves. That is also why an entry sometimes records a limit or a caveat the submission did not mention: we describe the product as published, not as pitched.

Where something is unclear, we ask rather than guess. A short reply with a link to the right documentation page usually settles it.

Most declines are about fit, not quality

The readers here are marketers researching software they are about to pay for. A tool can be genuinely good and still be wrong for this list: developer tooling, consumer apps and general business software all get turned down regularly. If yours is one of those, we say so plainly rather than leave the submission sitting unanswered.

The other common decline is timing. Products that have not shipped yet cannot be described accurately, and an entry written from a landing page ages badly the moment the real thing launches. Send it again once it is out.

Website URL
A URL to the product website or a product page on your company's website.

Software development agencies.
Landing pages with an email form for a waiting list.
Products that are not released yet will be rejected immediately.
Products using free subdomains (e.g. my-cool-app.vercel.com; myproduct.saasify.com).
Products that are not in English.

SaaS, IaaS & PaaS products and services.

Mobile apps (with decent websites).
Websites and services that are leaders in a specific niche (e.g. Airbnb).

Sometimes we could be a bit too liberal or relaxed when approving products. However, we preserve the right to reject or remove products even if they have been approved already.

Frequently Asked Questions

Have more questions? Don't hesitate to contact us here

What is Toolfolio, and who will see my tool?
Toolfolio is a curated directory and marketplace that helps people discover the best tools for productivity, design, AI, and startup growth. Your listing is seen by our audience of makers, founders, designers, and developers who browse, search, and compare tools across categories. Millions of people have discovered software on Toolfolio, and our audience values the directory precisely because it’s curated — we only accept and list quality tools that genuinely solve problems.
How long does review and approval take?
Because Toolfolio is curated, every submission is reviewed before going live. Approval usually takes 24–48 hours, and you’ll be notified by email once your listing is approved.
What is "Thumbnail View" on mobile?
Thumbnail View controls how your listing appears to people browsing Toolfolio on a mobile device. It displays your custom thumbnail image just as it appears on the desktop page. By default, mobile listings show only the tool’s icon and name — but if you use any of our paid listing options, your thumbnail will display on mobile too, helping increase your click-through rate (CTR) on mobile.
Can I change my thumbnail multiple times?
Yes. Every listing on Toolfolio comes with access to the Toolmaker Dashboard, where you can make changes to your listing yourself at any time. We offer free claims for tools already listed on Toolfolio, plus two paid listing tiers, each with their own benefits. Companies on our Growth plan can upload up to 5 images in their listing.
Can I suggest which categories my listing appears in?
You can request preferred categories during submission, but final placement is decided by our team to ensure the best fit. We weigh your suggestions alongside relevance, audience match, and content type when finalizing placement. For further requests please contact dudu@toolfolio.com.
Do you offer tracking or reporting for campaigns?
Yes. Once you sign up and claim your tool or pay for a listing, you’ll get access to the Toolmaker Dashboard with built-in analytics. It shows your page views, outbound clicks, and bookmarks, and calculates your click-through rate. Growth plan members also see the countries, devices, browsers, and operating systems of the people viewing their listing.
What gets a submission approved or rejected?
We approve tools that are functional, relevant to our categories, and genuinely useful to our audience. Common reasons for rejection include broken links, incomplete information, misleading claims, duplicate listings, or content that violates our guidelines. You can find more in our listing guidelines. If you believe your tool was declined in error, contact us at dudu@toolfolio.com.
Can I list more than one product?
Yes. You can list multiple products and manage them all from a single Toolmaker Dashboard, with an at-a-glance overview of how each tool is performing on Toolfolio.
Will listing on Toolfolio help my SEO or traffic?
Listings include a link to your site and exposure to our monthly visitors and newsletter subscribers. While we can’t guarantee specific SEO or traffic outcomes, many tools see referral traffic and increased discovery after listing. It’s also worth noting that many content creators use Toolfolio as a source for the tools they feature in their content.
Can I edit my listing after it’s published?
Yes. Your Toolmaker Dashboard includes an editor for updating your listing details whenever you need. We also re-scan your website at intervals — how often depends on your listing plan — to keep your content in sync with what you’re shipping and help drive more traffic to your listing.
Do you offer refunds on paid listings?
All listing payments are final and non-refundable. For billing questions, contact dudu@toolfolio.com.
